result.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
result.summary: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. With a single front camera, AR-WAM achieves 91.5 PDMS after supervised training and 94.0 after reinforcement learning on NAVSIM-v1, outperforming the compared strong end-to-end world-action models. In a dynamic setting of continuous driving, supervised AR-WAM keeps its visual history across decisions and outperforms strong world-action baselines.

AI.brief_summary: AR-WAM 提出面向自动驾驶的高效流式 world-action 模型：以因果视频骨干增量更新视觉上下文并复用历史计算，单次前向取得未来特征来条件化轨迹生成，再用强化学习按驾驶奖励优化策略，在 NAVSIM-v1 上报告 PDMS 提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其因果骨干的增量潜状态复用与「单次前向预测未来特征再条件化生成」可能为 LVR 的潜状态更新、预测性工作区表示及替代迭代生成的成本问题提供可供核查的方法线索，但研究任务是驾驶轨迹而非多模态推理本身。
